subtitle_zh: 随着火车缓缓驶出史凯威，我们正式开始这段闻名世界的白隘口铁路之旅。
subtitle_en: As the train slowly leaves Skagway, our world-famous White Pass journey begins.

subtitle_zh: 这条铁路全长一百一十英里，修建于 1898 年至 1900 年的克朗代克淘金热时期。
subtitle_en: This 110-mile railway was built during the Klondike Gold Rush, from 1898 to 1900.

subtitle_zh: 当年，成千上万的淘金者正是从这里踏上前往加拿大育空地区的寻金之路。
subtitle_en: Thousands of gold seekers began their journey toward Canada's Yukon from here.

subtitle_zh: 短短二十多英里，我们就将从海平面一路攀升到接近三千英尺的白隘口。
subtitle_en: In just over twenty miles, we will climb from sea level to nearly 3,000 feet.

subtitle_zh: 这里是白隘口铁路的维修基地。
subtitle_en: This is the maintenance base for the White Pass railway.

subtitle_zh: 今天仍然负责维护铁路的机车和客车。
subtitle_en: It still maintains the railway's locomotives and passenger cars today.

subtitle_zh: 百年前，这里同样是整个铁路系统的重要后勤中心，保证列车能够安全穿越这片险峻的山区。
subtitle_en: A century ago, it was also a key support center for safe mountain operations.

subtitle_zh: 这里是著名的淘金热公墓。
subtitle_en: This is the famous Gold Rush Cemetery.

subtitle_zh: 长眠于这里的不仅有普通居民，也包括臭名昭著的索比·史密斯，以及在枪战中击毙他的英雄 Frank Reid。
subtitle_en: Among those buried here are Soapy Smith and Frank Reid, who killed him in a gunfight.

subtitle_zh: 这座安静的墓园，也见证着淘金时代混乱而传奇的一段历史。
subtitle_en: This quiet cemetery witnessed a chaotic and legendary part of the Gold Rush era.

subtitle_zh: 火车跨越史凯威河东支，来到丹佛地区。
subtitle_en: The train crosses the east fork of the Skagway River and enters the Denver area.

subtitle_zh: 附近有一条著名的步道，可以一直通往丹佛冰川。
subtitle_en: A nearby trail leads all the way toward Denver Glacier.

subtitle_zh: 随着海拔不断升高，远方开始出现冰川、雪山以及更加壮观的峡谷景色。
subtitle_en: As we climb higher, glaciers, snowy peaks, and deeper canyons begin to appear.

subtitle_zh: 这里就是著名的 Rocky Point。
subtitle_en: This is the famous Rocky Point.

subtitle_zh: 这里也是整条铁路最受欢迎的摄影地点之一。
subtitle_en: It is one of the most popular photo spots on the entire railway.

subtitle_zh: 向山谷望去，可以俯瞰整个史凯威方向，远处还能看到哈丁山以及哈丁冰川。
subtitle_en: Looking down the valley, we can see toward Skagway, Mount Harding, and Harding Glacier.

subtitle_zh: 随着火车不断攀升，海岸森林逐渐被裸露的岩石和高山植被所取代。
subtitle_en: As the train climbs, coastal forest gives way to bare rock and alpine plants.
